==English==

===Pronunciation===
{{multiple images
|direction = vertical
|image1 = D'Nealian Cursive.svg
|caption1 = [[cursive|Cursive]] script letters ''(sense 1)'' of the English [[alphabet]], together with some [[punctuation mark]]s and [[number#Noun|numbers]]
|image2 = Letter MET DP7461.jpg
|caption2 = A letter ''(sense 2)'' written in the early 19th century
}}

* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛtə/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-letter.ogg|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛtɚ/|[-ɾɚ]|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-letter.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈletə/|[-ɾə]|a=AusE}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈlɛʈ(ː)əʳ/|a=Indic}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛtə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|let|ter}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|letter}}, {{m|enm|lettre}}, from {{der|en|fro|letre}}, from {{der|en|la|littera||letter of the alphabet"; ''in plural'', "epistle}}. {{displaced|ang|bōcstæf|lit=book staff}} in sense 1 and {{m|ang|ǣrendġewrit|lit=message writing}} in sense 2.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|lettre||obsolete}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q9788}} A [[symbol]] in an [[alphabet]].
#: {{hyper|en|grapheme#Noun|symbol#Noun}}
#: {{cot|en|q1=nonalphabetical characters|numeral#Noun|digit#Noun|number#Noun|punctuation mark#Noun|word space#Noun|white space#Noun}}
#: {{ux|en|There are twenty-six '''letters''' in the English alphabet.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|23|38|passage=And a superscription also was written ouer him in '''letters''' of Greeke, and Latin, & Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE IEWES.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q133492}} A written or printed communication, usually defined as longer and more formal than a [[note]]. {{n-g|(Sometimes specifically one that is on [[paper]]<!--either [[handwritten]] or [[printed out]]--><!--archetypically so, for a personal missive, but not so much anymore regarding, for example, public letters from a government agency as PDFs published online-->.)}}
#: {{hyper|en|message#Noun|;|document#Noun}}
#: {{cot|en|note#Noun|email#Noun|text message#Noun}}
#: {{ux|en|I wrote a '''letter''' to my sister about my life.}}
#: {{ux|en|Let's head the '''letter''' with the company's logo.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author={{w|William Walsh (poet)|William Walsh}}|passage=The style of '''letters''' ought to be free, easy, and natural.|title='''Letters''' and Poems, Amorous and Gallant|chapter=Preface|year=1692}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|title=Poet Lore: A Magazine of Letters|volume=4|publisher=AMS Reprint Company|location=New York, N.Y.|editors=w:Charlotte Porter; w:Helen A. Clarke|author=''P.A.C.''|section={{w|Longfellow|Henry Wadsworth Longfellow}}’s ‘Golden Legend’ and its Analogues|oclc=6524500|page=94|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=LUHKPKjW-ZEC&pg=PA94#v=onepage&q&f=false|passage=The magician gave this to the young man and said to him,“ Go at such an hour of the night and stand before a pagan tomb and call the demons, and throw the '''letter''' into the air, and immediately they will come to you.” And the young  man called the devils and threw the '''letter''' into the air, and the prince of darkness came,{{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=He read the '''letter''' aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement.}}
#* {{RQ:Christie Autobiography|I|4|passage=An indulgent playmate, Grannie would lay aside the long scratchy-looking '''letter''' she was writing (heavily crossed ‘to save notepaper’) and enter into the delightful pastime of ‘a chicken from Mr Whiteley's’.}}
# The [[literal]] [[meaning]] of something, as distinguished from its [[intended]] and [[remote]]r meaning (the {{m|en|spirit}}).
#* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|chapter=Of Obedience|section=I (Of Obedience to our Superiours)|page=183|passage=In obedience to humane laws, we muſt obſerve the '''letter''' of the Law, where we can without doing violence to the reaſon of the Law and the intention of the Law-giver: but where they croſſe each other, the charity of the Law is to be preferred before its diſcipline, and the reaſon of it before the '''letter'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson Princess|IV|81|passage=I broke the '''letter''' of it to keep the sense.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=23 February 2009|title=Euro MP expenses 'can reach £1m'|author=Laurence Peter|work=w:BBC News|quotee={{w|Chris Davies (Liberal Democrat politician)|Chris Davies}}|passage=Some MEPs from some countries may have pocketed £2m more than I have by observing the '''letter''' but not the spirit of the rules.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110200805/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/7904886.stm}}
# {{lb|en|in the plural}} [[literature|Literature]].
#: {{ux|en|Benjamin Franklin was multiskilled – a scientist, politician and a man of '''letters'''.}}
# {{lb|en|law}} A [[division]] [[unit]] of a piece of law marked by a letter of the [[alphabet]].
#: {{uxi|en|'''Letter''' (b) constitutes an exception to this provision.}}
# {{senseid|en|US paper size}}{{lb|en|US|uncountable}} A size of [[paper]], 8½ [[inch|in]] × 11 in (215.9 [[millimetre|mm]] × 279.4 mm).
#: {{syn|en|short bond paper}}
# {{lb|en|Canada|uncountable}} A size of [[paper]], 215 mm × 280 mm.
# {{lb|en|US|scholastic}} {{clipping of|en|varsity letter}}.
# {{lb|en|printing|dated}} A single [[type]]; type, collectively; a style of type.
#* {{RQ:Evelyn Diary|volume=I|entrydate=8 February 1644|page=41|passage=Under these, thro’ a garden in which is an ample fountaine, was the King's printing-house, and that famous '''letter''' so much esteem’d.}}
